summary: Feed s111_double is degraded: 17.6% of TCP sessions are one-way and 13.2% of frames are sliced to ~192 bytes. IDS requires both directions and full payload for stateful signature detection.

findings.root_cause: Only one direction of TCP sessions is reaching the IDS. Most likely the packet broker is forwarding a single SPAN/mirror direction or asymmetric TAP feeds without aggregating both sides, or flow-based load-balancing is splitting client->server and server->client to different tools.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs both directions for TCP state tracking, stream reassembly and request/response correlation. With 24/136 sessions one-way, it will miss handshakes, fail to reassemble streams, miss exploits and generate inaccurate alerts.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each bidirectional flow to the same IDS tool port so stateful detection sees full session.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker slicing/snaplen is enabled and cutting frames to ~192 bytes, likely to save bandwidth or fit tool capacity. 257 of 1948 frames (13.2%) are truncated.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs full payload for signature matching, file extraction and exploit detection. Sliced frames strip L7 payload, making the IDS blind to application-layer attacks even when it sees both directions.

recommended_fix.why: IDS requires full payload up to 1518 bytes per tool profile; disable slicing or increase snaplen to at least max_frame_bytes so signatures can inspect complete packets.
